title: Mini-cohort bridged rollout with telemetry-led commit and reversible snapshotting
author: Sofia Chen
release_notes: Adds a lightweight bridged rollout controller for mini-cohorts with telemetry-gated commits and snapshot-based reversible swap. Improves safety for low-traffic canaries and provides richer telemetry for rollback decisions.
description:
Context: small traffic experiments (mini-cohorts and transient A/B tests) needed a lower-overhead, reversible rollout primitive that still provides telemetry-driven safety guarantees. The existing orchestrator is tuned for larger cohort waves and introduces operational cost/handoffs for very low-traffic experiments. This PR introduces a 'bridged' rollout controller optimized for mini-cohorts: it can transition shadowed traffic into live canary lanes via a telemetry-led commit, take atomic reversible snapshots of routing state and cache pointers, and provide a deferred-commit window for manual verification.
Motivation: make micro-experiments safe and cheap to run in production while preserving fast rollback with minimal state reconciliation.
Summary of changes: 1) controllers/bridged_rollout_controller.go: new controller implementing the bridged lifecycle (observe -> shadow-bridge -> staged-swap -> telemetry-commit -> reversible-snapshot). 2) api/rollout_v1alpha1_types.go: schema for BridgedRollout resource (miniCohortSelector, commitConditions, snapshotPolicy). 3) cli/rolloutctl: added `bridge apply|promote|revert` commands and safety flags (--defer-window, --telemetry-hysteresis). 4) runtime/router: snapshot and swap hooks to capture routing entries and KV cache reference frames atomically. 5) observability/dashboards: new Grafana panels for mini-cohort heatmap, commit decision trace, and a prebuilt alert rule (bridged_rollout_commit_lag). 6) integration tests/e2e: added low-traffic simulation harness and deterministic metrics generator. 7) docs: rollout patterns doc and CLI quickstart.
Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] CLI and API changes with validation - [x] Snapshot + swap runtime hooks - [x] Integration tests for rollback and partial-commit cases - [x] Docs and example quickstart - [x] Helm chart bump for rollout controller image - [x] Benchmarks for overhead at 100qps and 5rps.
Commits: ["init bridged rollout controller and API types","add router snapshot hooks and atomic swap primitives","implement telemetry-led commit logic with hysteresis","cli rolloutctl bridge glue and validation","integration tests: mini-cohort low-traffic harness","docs: bridged rollout patterns and dashboard templates"]. Files changed (high level): ["controllers/bridged_rollout_controller.go","api/rollout_v1alpha1_types.go","runtime/router/snapshot.go","cli/rolloutctl/bridge.go","observability/dashboards/bridged-rollout.json","charts/redwood-controllers/values.yaml","tests/e2e/bridged_rollout_test.go","docs/rollouts/bridged.md","pkg/telemetry/decision_trace.go"]. Performance note: added microbench showing average 2.3ms extra p99 latency when capturing lightweight snapshots during quiescent windows; memory overhead ~6MB per controller for snapshot references.
Safety and rollback: snapshots store pointers to router and KV cache frames in a reversible snapshot store; revert re-applies snapshots atomically and triggers a verification probe to ensure KV cache consistency; commit condition uses metric gates (latency_p50, error_rate, generation_quality_score) with configurable hysteresis windows.
Migration: API is v1alpha1; no in-place incompatible changes to existing rollout CRDs; helm chart bumped to register new controller.
Backports: squash-merged and cherry-picked to release/2026-01 for customers using early-mini-cohort pilots.
Related work: ties into ENG-4894 (low-traffic experiment infra) and ENG-5031 (snapshot store for router), follow-up planned for multi-arm expansion.

review_comments: Ravi: Can you explain how snapshot pointers remain valid across scale-down events? Author: The snapshot captures a stable identifier set and a lightweight pointer to cache frames; on scale-down we keep a tombstone mapping for up to 15m to allow rehydrate+verify before reclaiming memory.
Leah: Suggest tightening default hysteresis for error_rate to avoid noisy commits at 1% variance. Author: tightened to 3-sample window and made it configurable via commitConditions.hysteresisSamples.
Ethan: Add a safety gate to disallow commit if background validation probes have >1% mismatch. Author: added validationProbe field to schema and tests to cover mismatch path.
Ravi: CI flake in e2e that relied on time.Sleep; can we replace with a readiness hook? Author: replaced with readiness-based wait and reran tests.
Leah (approve): Verified dashboards and smoke-tested with local e2e harness. Approving to merge.
Ethan (approve): Verified rollback scenarios and reverted snapshot reapply path. Approving to merge.
merge_outcome: PR was squash-merged into main on 2026-01-25 after CI green and two approvals. Changes were cherry-picked to release/2026-01 for pilot customers. No incidents reported during initial ramp. Monitoring: bridged_rollout_commit_lag alerted once during a noisy traffic window and auto-reverted per policy; follow-up ticket created ENG-5109 to refine alert thresholds.
notes_for_release: Feature: bridged rollout controller (v1alpha1) for mini-cohort experiments. How to use: see docs/rollouts/bridged.md and rolloutctl quickstart. Backport: release/2026-01. Operational impact: enable controller via helm flag controllers.bridgedRollout.enabled=true. Rollout plan: enable for internal pilot at 1% of teams for 2 weeks, monitor commit_lag and decision_trace metrics.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: stale snapshot pointers after aggressive autoscaling could theoretically lead to failed revert operations. Mitigation: tombstone window, pre-revert verification probes, and automatic soft-fallback to traffic-holdpoint on verification failure. We also implemented canary-level circuit-breaker to abort commit if validation probes exceed threshold.
